definitions: The legal right, established by usage or grant, to pass along a specific route through property belonging to another.
A path or thoroughfare subject to such a right.
The right of a vehicle or pedestrian to proceed ahead of another in a particular situation or at a particular place.
Land or property acquired for a transportation or utility corridor.
examples: The utility company has a right-of-way across the farm.
The pedestrian always has the right-of-way.
They are clearing the right-of-way for the new pipeline.
The train tracks run along the old right-of-way.
